original_question: For the average mixing matrix Mc of a graph, determine exactly when its non-negative rank is equal to n, the number of vertices. Here the non-negative rank of a non-negative n x n matrix M is the least integer k such that M can be written as a sum of k rank-1 matrices with non-negative entries.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Open Problem 4.2 of the arXiv version; in the later published version this is renumbered as Open Problem 4.3, and its first sentence is the same core question: "When is the non-negative rank of \widehat M equal to n?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target object—the average mixing matrix of a graph—and the target extremal property, namely whether its non-negative rank equals n, the number of vertices. It also uses the same decomposition-style definition of non-negative rank that the paper states. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
missing_details: The paper’s notation is \widehat M, not M_c. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

To make the question stand-alone, you should define the continuous-time quantum walk and the average mixing matrix: U(t)=e^{itA(G)}, M(t)=U(t)\circ U(-t), and \widehat M=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T M(t)\,dt=\sum_r E_r\circ E_r when A(G)=\sum_r \theta_r E_r. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
It should state explicitly that G is a finite graph on n=|V(G)| vertices, so \widehat M is an n\times n real entrywise nonnegative matrix. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

It should make explicit that the non-negative rank is taken over \mathbb{R}: one seeks a decomposition into entrywise nonnegative real n\times n matrices of ordinary rank 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

No extra hypotheses such as distance-regularity, primitivity, or simple spectrum should be added here; those belong to neighboring open problems or lemmas, not to this non-negative-rank problem itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
refined_question: Let G be a finite graph on n=|V(G)| vertices with adjacency matrix A(G)=\sum_{r=0}^d \theta_r E_r. Define U(t)=e^{itA(G)}, M(t)=U(t)\circ U(-t), and the average mixing matrix \widehat M=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T M(t)\,dt=\sum_{r=0}^d E_r\circ E_r, where \circ denotes the Schur product. Characterize those graphs G for which the non-negative rank of \widehat M, defined by \operatorname{rank}_+(\widehat M)=\min\{k: \widehat M=\sum_{s=1}^k N_s,\ N_s\in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n\times n},\ \operatorname{rank}(N_s)=1\}, is equal to n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s intended problem. Section 4 defines the average mixing matrix \widehat M from the time-averaged mixing matrices and gives the spectral-idempotent formula for it; Section 4.1 then defines non-negative rank and immediately asks exactly when that non-negative rank equals n. Nearby remarks about ordinary rank, simple eigenvalues, complete positivity, cpsd-rank, and cp-rank are contextual motivations, not extra hypotheses or equivalent reformulations of this specific open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
